2608.19436.title: Longitudinal Bayesian Learning of Continuous Disease Position across the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum
2608.19436.paper_summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) progresses as a continuous biological process, whereas most existing neuroimaging-based artificial intelligence methods remain limited to discrete diagnosis or clinical score prediction from cross-sectional imaging. In this work, we propose Disease Continuum Positioning (DCP), a longitudinal Bayesian Learning framework that continuously estimates disease severity from longitudinal diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). Specifically, DCP models disease severity as a low-dimensional probabilistic latent variable by jointly integrating longitudinal observations with weak clinical supervision, from which the proposed Disease Continuum Score (DCS) is derived to quantify an individual's position along the Alzheimer's disease continuum together with its associated uncertainty. Extensive experiments on the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort demonstrate that DCP consistently outperforms representative disease progression methods. More importantly, comprehensive validation analyses show that DCS accurately characterizes disease severity, exhibits strong clinical relevance, preserves longitudinal disease evolution, and predicts future disease conversion. These results suggest that DCS provides a quantitative imaging-derived representation for continuous assessment of Alzheimer's disease progression beyond conventional diagnostic labels and clinical scores.
2608.19436.paper_summary_zh: 阿茲海默症（AD）作為一個連續的生物過程而進展，而大多數現有的基於神經影像的人工智慧方法仍然僅限於從橫斷面影像進行離散診斷或臨床評分預測。在這項工作中，我們提出了疾病連續性定位（DCP），這是一個長期的貝葉斯學習框架，能夠從長期擴散張量影像（DTI）中持續估計疾病的嚴重性。具體而言，DCP將疾病的嚴重性建模為一個低維的概率潛在變量，通過將長期觀察與弱臨床監督共同整合，從中推導出所提出的疾病連續性評分（DCS），以量化個體在阿茲海默症連續體中的位置及其相關的不確定性。對阿茲海默症神經影像倡議（ADNI）隊列的廣泛實驗表明，DCP始終優於代表性的疾病進展方法。更重要的是，全面的驗證分析顯示，DCS準確地表徵了疾病的嚴重性，展現出強大的臨床相關性，保留了長期的疾病演變，並預測未來的疾病轉變。這些結果表明，DCS提供了一種定量的影像衍生表示，用於超越傳統診斷標籤和臨床評分的阿茲海默症進展的連續評估。
